findings.element: src/tasks.js onKey() — the keyboard carry; Space branch l.2924-2969, Enter branch l.2972-2991, endCarry() l.2639, pointerdown guard l.4442
findings.problem: A keyboard carry mutates the board on every arrow (carryMove -> moveTo), but only ONE of its five exits records the move. Driven at 1440 on tasks.board: Space on demo-t-01 (aria-grabbed=true, data-force=moving), ArrowRight (the card is now in In progress — the model has already changed), then: (a) Enter — opens the task panel, says only 'Task open.', and Ctrl+Z answers 'Nothing left to undo.'; (b) Tab — same, undo empty, focus moves to the tick inside the same card; (c) a rail switch to Notes and back — same, undo empty; (d) a pointer press on empty lane ground — endCarry() runs and says '...put down in the in progress column.', and Ctrl+Z still answers 'Nothing left to undo.' Only Space calls arm() and only Escape reverts. In (a), (b) and (c) carriedId is never cleared either, so aria-grabbed="true" and data-force="moving" stay on the card — 2px indigo outline + 1.5px indigo ring + 5px halo + lift + scale(1.02), the loudest treatment on the board — with document.activeElement === BODY, until an unrelated repaint clears it. The comment above endCarry() (l.2632-2638) states this class was already fixed and names Tab away specifically; endCarry() is wired to pointerdown only.
findings.fix: Lift the Space branch's commit block (l.2926-2969: the completed() / put-it-back-is-a-non-event / arm()+say() decision, then carriedId = null; carriedFrom = null) into a commitCarry() function, and route every exit through it. (1) In endCarry() (l.2639) call commitCarry() instead of the bare say('...put down...') so the pointer exit arms an undo too. (2) In the Enter branch (l.2972) call endCarry() before openCard(id, ...). (3) On the board host add a focusout guard mirroring the pointerdown one at l.4442: if carriedId and the incoming relatedTarget is not inside .card[data-id=carriedId], call endCarry() then mount(). (4) Call endCarry() from the suite's product-switch handler in src/app.js before the deck changes product. After the change every exit either commits with an armed undo and a receipt, or cancels — and none can leave aria-grabbed/data-force set.

findings.problem: .cardDots grows a 24px mark into its touch target with padding: 10px + margin: -13px -10px -13px auto and box-sizing: content-box. The negative right margin pulls the box back visually, but negative margins do not shrink an ancestor's scrollable overflow, so the dots' border box (measured right edge 359px) sits past .trayBody's content edge (330px) and gives every populated lane a phantom horizontal scroll region. Measured on a fresh page, no interaction, tasks.dense: scrollWidth-clientWidth per lane is [0,0,0,0,0] @1440, [3,4,0,0,0] @1400, [11,12,2,0,0] @1360, [19,20,10,0,0] @1320, [27,28,18,0,0] @1280, [43,44,34,0,0] @1200. tasks.board @1280 [13,14,4,0,0]; tasks.compact @1200 [11,12,0,0,0]. It is user-reachable: a single page.mouse.wheel(80, 0) over the To do lane at 1280 sets scrollLeft to 27/27, after which the whole column has slid left, the first card's tick circle is sliced in half by the lane's left edge, the ... menu is exposed, and the column is visibly out of register with its own 'TO DO 10' heading, which did not move. No fade, no snap, nothing in the scrolled region. 1280 is one of the five declared gate viewports and 1200 is one pixel above the board's own declared 1199 floor.
findings.fix: Add overflow-x: clip to [data-app="tasks"] .trayBody (it already sets overflow-y: auto). Unlike hidden, clip creates no scroll container in X, so neither a wheel gesture nor a future scroll-into-view can shift the lane. Clipping happens at the padding box (122-336px at 1280) while cards sit at 128-330 and card outlines reach 124-334, so nothing visible is lost. If the outline margin is wanted, add overflow-clip-margin: 4px. Leave .cardDots' geometry alone — the target size is correct and the fix belongs on the scroller.

findings.problem: Every other count on the sheet restates itself under a filter — lanes become 'To do, 0 of 3 shown' with a visible '0/3', and the empty board says 'No overdue task is on the board for Mara & Finn. All 13 are hidden.' The head's completion meter does not. With the client filter and the overdue chip both on and zero cards showing, the head still reads '5 of 13 done — 38%' with the pace bar filled, and [role=meter] still carries aria-valuenow=5, aria-valuemax=13 and aria-label '5 of 13 done, 38 percent', unqualified. The one object on the head that looks like progress is the only number on the sheet still describing a different set, and it is the loudest quantitative mark on an empty board. Same in the List view.
findings.fix: While filtering() is true, recompute the meter over the filtered set and say so in the same grammar the lanes use: visible text '3 of 7 done' with the bar drawn from the filtered numbers, and aria-valuemin/max/now set from them, with the accessible name appended with the scope — e.g. '3 of 7 done, 43 percent, for Mara & Finn'. When a filter leaves nothing on the board, drop the bar to zero and set the name to 'Nothing shown' rather than leaving the unfiltered figure standing. Restore the whole-board figures the moment filtering() goes false, which the existing filter-clear path already repaints.

findings.element: span.sr#cd-<id> built at src/tasks.js l.461 as the card's aria-describedby target
findings.problem: The string that exists only to be the card's accessible description is left in the reading order. page.accessibility.snapshot() on one board card returns: article name 'Confirm marquee sides with the hire company'; article description 'Mara & Finn, Saturday. ... Mara & Finn. High priority.'; then as children a paragraph carrying the title a second time, a generic node carrying the whole description string a second time (the .sr span itself), a paragraph carrying the note a third time, a button carrying the tag a third time, and text carrying 'High'/'priority' a third time. .sr hides the node from sight, not from assistive technology. Thirteen cards on the board, thirty-two in dense — browsing the board reads roughly three times the content it has. Round 6 fixed exactly this on the seam's card ('does not say it twice to a screen reader either') and left it on every board card.
findings.fix: Add aria-hidden="true" to the describedby target at src/tasks.js l.461: '<span class="sr" aria-hidden="true" id="cd-' + esc(task.id) + '">'. aria-describedby resolves its text from aria-hidden subtrees, so the description survives intact while the duplicate leaves the reading order, and the visible note, tag and priority are then each spoken once.

findings.problem: l.448 emits aria-roledescription="Movable task" only when the task is not done; l.449 emits aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight" unconditionally. Driven: all five cards in the Done lane report aria-roledescription null with the shortcuts still attached, and they are fully movable — Space then ArrowLeft on demo-t-09 carried it into Waiting (and the roledescription reappeared the moment it left Done). So five of the board's thirteen cards advertise a set of shortcuts to a screen reader with no word for what those shortcuts operate, while behaving identically to the eight that do.
findings.fix: Emit the roledescription unconditionally: change (done ? "" : ' aria-roledescription="Movable task"') at l.448 to ' aria-roledescription="Movable task"'. The card is movable in both states, so the name should say so in both.

biggestWin: The suite's central claim is not a caption, it is measurable and it holds. With a 45-character draft half-typed in .topField and the Notes index scrolled to 260px, switching Notes -> Tasks -> Timeline -> Notes on the rail returns the draft byte-identical and the index scrollTop still at exactly 260 — nothing is torn down, nothing is lost. Around that, the craft that automation cannot see is genuinely at the benchmark: Space on the tick is explicitly guarded so it ticks instead of picking the card up (the worst hijack class, defended in a comment at l.2916); the roving model reaches all 32 cards in dense with none stranded; the filter states itself in every lane label, offers exactly one way out when it empties the screen, and Escape unwinds it one press at a time with an honest sentence each time; the dictation floor's focus trap is airtight over 28 tabs; Notes and Timeline hold focus and every scroller through a 1920-768-1920 sweep; and I drove every state at five widths with zero console errors.
